records.issue_text: `from_dict` cannot round-trip a JSON-serialized dict because `queued` arrives as a string, and the caught TypeError returns None, silently disabling cycle protection
records.rationale: The diff’s `AssignmentSource.from_dict` simply does `return cls(**input_dict)` and only returns `None` on `(ValueError, TypeError)`. Passing a JSON-decoded `queued` value as a string would not inherently raise either error because Python dataclasses don’t enforce type annotations at runtime, so `cls(queued="...")` will typically succeed. Therefore the claimed mechanism (“queued arrives as a string” -> “TypeError” -> `None` -> “cycle protection disabled”) is contradicted by `return cls(**input_dict)` and the narrow exceptions caught.
